classes.name: Elección de Presidente de la República
classes.note: Direct election by absolute majority of valid votes; otherwise a second round between the two leaders on the fourth Sunday after (CPR art. 26). Four-year term without immediate re-election since 2005 (art. 25); Aylwin served four years (1990-1994) and Frei and Lagos six (Ley 19.295). Chileans abroad vote since 2017 (LOC 18.700 art. 190). Contests count rounds: each second round is its own contest.

classes.name: Elección presidencial directa bajo la Constitución de 1925
classes.note: The 1925 Constitution made the presidential election direct, for six years without immediate re-election; when no candidate won an absolute majority the Congreso Pleno chose between the two leaders (class presidente_congreso_pleno). Eleven elections, from 24 October 1925 to 4 September 1970, by province and department; women voted from 1952.
classes.finest_note: comuna or department in the Dirección del Registro Electoral's printed returns

classes.name: Elección presidencial por el Congreso Pleno
classes.name_en: President chosen by the joint Congress when no candidate won a majority, 1925-1973
classes.note: Under the 1925 Constitution the Congreso Pleno chose between the two candidates with the most votes when none had an absolute majority (1946, 1952, 1958, and 1970).

dates.note: Not yet enumerated from the Congress's session records.

classes.name: Elección presidencial indirecta por electores (1826-1920)
classes.note: Under the constitutions of 1828 and 1833 voters chose presidential electors by department, and the electors chose the president; Congress decided when no candidate had an absolute majority of electors. The last such election was in 1920.

dates.note: Not yet enumerated; the BCN timeline does not list presidential elections before 1952.

classes.name: Elección de Diputados
classes.note: The whole chamber is renewed every four years (CPR art. 47). 1989-2013: 120 deputies, two per district in 60 districts, by the binomial system (D'Hondt between lists); since 2017: 155 deputies in 28 districts of 3 to 8 seats by D'Hondt with open lists and gender quotas (LOC 18.700 arts. 178-179 bis). There are no by-elections: a vacancy is filled by the party.

classes.name: Plebiscitos comunales
classes.note: The mayor with the council's agreement, or at the initiative of the commune's voters, puts local investment, planning, or administration questions to a binding plebiscite held on a Sunday 120 days after the decree, run by Servel; binding if more than half the electorate votes (LOC 18.695 arts. 99-104; LOC 18.700 art. 169). Known ones include Vitacura (15 March 2009), Peñalolén (2011), and San Pedro de la Paz (29 September 2019).

classes.name: Alcaldes elegidos por el concejo o por la votación de concejales (1992-2000)
classes.name_en: Mayors chosen by the council or from the councillor vote, 1992-2000
classes.note: From 1992 to 2000 mayors had no ballot of their own: the council chose one of its members, or the most-voted councillor became mayor when the thresholds the law set were met.
classes.disposition_reason: No separate ballot: the mayor was chosen by the council or followed from the councillor vote, which the class concejo_municipal holds.

classes.name: Elecciones municipales de regidores (hasta 1973)
classes.note: Municipalities elected regidores from the nineteenth century (the Ley de Comuna Autónoma of 24 December 1891 gave them control of elections); women voted in municipal elections from Ley 5.357 of 1934. The last were held in April 1971; the junta dissolved the councils in 1973 and appointed mayors until 1992.
classes.locator: https://www.bcn.cl/historiapolitica/elecciones/index.html?periodo=1925-1973

dates.note: Not yet enumerated; the BCN timeline lists the laws but not the municipal election days.

classes.name: Elecciones primarias presidenciales
classes.note: Servel runs a joint national primary for President and parliamentarians on the twentieth Sunday before the presidential election, open to parties and pacts that opt in; the result binds the parties (Ley 20.640 art. 3). One contest per pact. 2021 was held on 18 July under a pandemic transitory rule.
classes.locator: https://www.bcn.cl/leychile/navegar?idNorma=1107657 (art. 3: "deberá realizarse el vigésimo domingo anterior a la fecha de la elección de Presidente de la República")

classes.name: Elecciones internas de los partidos políticos
classes.note: Parties elect their organs and may nominate by internal procedures under their statutes (Ley 18.603); only the Ley 20.640 primaries are run by Servel.
classes.disposition_reason: Run by the parties themselves under their statutes, not by Servel; no official public results.

classes.name: Elecciones de directivas de juntas de vecinos
classes.note: Each junta de vecinos elects its board among its members, under the supervision of a ministro de fe; disputes go to the regional electoral court (Ley 19.418).
classes.disposition_reason: Membership organizations' internal elections under Ley 19.418, run by the organizations and not by Servel; electorates are their members, not the electoral roll.

classes.name: Elección de consejeros nacionales indígenas de CONADI
classes.name_en: Indigenous members of the CONADI National Council
classes.note: Eight indigenous representatives (four Mapuche, one Aymara, one Atacameño, one Rapa Nui, and one urban) sit on CONADI's council for four years; CONADI holds a vote among registered indigenous people to propose them.
classes.locator: https://www.bcn.cl/leychile/navegar?idNorma=30620 (art. 41 d: "Estos serán designados, a propuesta de las Comunidades y Asociaciones Indígenas, por el Presidente de la República")
classes.disposition_reason: By law the President designates the eight on the communities' proposal; the vote CONADI organizes is a consultation it runs itself, not an election administered by Servel.
